transcript.text: *Looks up from a ledger, adjusting spectacles* Good afternoon, sir. Welcome to Finch & Son. I’m afraid Mr. Finch is away on business—won’t be back for a few weeks, I’m told. Can I help you with something in his stead?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, good afternoon. I am Abraham Lincoln, and I have come to discuss the suit that Mr. Finch was to have tailored for me. Unfortunately, there are some issues with the stitching, the sleeve lengths, and the quality of the fabric. I had hoped to address these concerns with Mr. Finch directly, but as he is away, I must bring them to your attention instead.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Nods slowly, expression turning apologetic but firm* Ah, Mr. Lincoln. I recall your order—a fine black broadcloth suit, if I’m not mistaken. I’m sorry to hear you’re dissatisfied, but I must inform you that all custom orders are final upon pickup. The receipt you signed states clearly that no alterations or refunds are given once the garment leaves the shop.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I understand your policy, but I must insist that the quality of the suit I received does not meet the standards that were promised to me. The stitching is crooked, one sleeve is noticeably shorter than the other, and the fabric is not the quality of black broadcloth that I paid for. I trust that Mr. Finch would want to uphold the reputation of his establishment by ensuring that his customers are satisfied with their purchases.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Shifts uncomfortably, but maintains a polite, resolute tone* I do sympathize, sir, truly. But Mr. Finch was very clear about the terms. He always says, “A man’s signature is his bond.” You inspected the suit upon collection and signed the receipt. I’m not authorized to make exceptions, even for a gentleman of your standing.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I appreciate your adherence to Mr. Finch's policies, but I must stress the importance of integrity in craftsmanship. It is not just about the signature on a piece of paper, but about delivering on the promises made to a customer. I trust that Mr. Finch would want his customers to be satisfied with the work done by his shop. I urge you to reconsider and make the necessary adjustments to the suit.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Sighs softly, looking down at the ledger before meeting his eyes* Mr. Lincoln, I understand your position—truly I do. But I’m just the assistant, minding the shop. I haven’t the skill to alter a suit of that make, and Mr. Finch left no instructions for exceptions. The policy is there to protect the shop from… well, from changes of mind after the fact. I’m afraid my hands are tied.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I appreciate your candor, sir, and I understand the predicament you find yourself in. It seems we have reached an impasse. While I may not be able to sway your decision today, I trust that when Mr. Finch returns, he will consider the reputation of his establishment and the importance of upholding the quality of his work. Thank you for your time and attention to this matter.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Nods respectfully, a trace of relief in his expression* Thank you for your understanding, Mr. Lincoln. I’ll make sure to pass along your concerns when Mr. Finch returns. Safe travels to you, sir.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, sir. I appreciate your willingness to convey my concerns to Mr. Finch upon his return. I bid you good day and safe travels as well.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Bows slightly* Good day to you, Mr. Lincoln. Do take care.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Good day to you as well. Thank you, and farewell.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
